content.value_statement: React Native teams often repeat component, state, and data-fetching decisions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a compact reference for proven TypeScript patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains reusable React and React Native component patterns, including custom hooks, compound components, and render props.
Shows state management choices for local state, context, and Zustand stores.
Demonstrates data fetching with loading, error handling, and cleanup for React effects.
Summarizes performance patterns such as memoization, stable callbacks, and lazy loading.
Covers mobile UI concerns such as safe areas and keyboard avoiding views.
limitations: The skill is a reference guide and does not inspect a project automatically.
Examples are concise and may need adaptation for a specific codebase.
It focuses on React Native and TypeScript, not native iOS or Android internals.
It does not include automated tests, scripts, or dependency installation steps.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Choose a component and state pattern before implementing a React Native screen.

use_cases.title: Refactor Repeated Logic
use_cases.description: Move duplicated behavior into custom hooks or shared components with clearer boundaries.

use_cases.title: Review App Quality
use_cases.description: Check a React Native feature for loading states, cleanup, error handling, and mobile layout concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Component Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a React Native feature. Help me choose between a custom hook, compound components, and render props. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor State Management
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Native state flow and recommend whether local state, context, or a Zustand store fits best. Explain the migration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Data Fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me improve a React Native data-fetching hook. Focus on loading states, error handling, cancellation, and readable TypeScript.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Feature Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Native feature design for component boundaries, performance risks, state ownership, mobile layout concerns, and testing priorities.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to reuse modal open and close logic across several screens.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends extracting a custom hook with clear state ownership and a simple toggle API.

output_examples.input: A team needs to share the current user across many React Native screens.
output_examples.output: The skill compares context and a lightweight global store, then recommends the simpler option based on update frequency.

output_examples.input: A screen fetches user data and sometimes updates state after the user leaves the screen.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests effect cleanup, explicit loading and error states, and a safer data-fetching flow.

best_practices: Use the smallest pattern that solves the current problem clearly.
Add loading, error, and cleanup behavior when data or effects are involved.
Profile performance issues before adding memoization or lazy loading.
anti_patterns: Do not create large components that mix layout, data fetching, and business rules.
Do not move state to a global store before local state and context are insufficient.
Do not optimize every render path without measuring the real performance cost.

faq.question: What projects is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for React Native projects that use TypeScript and common React patterns.

faq.question: Does it write complete application code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and guidance. Complete code still needs project-specific context.

faq.question: Can it help with state management choices?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares local state, context, and lightweight global state patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover React Native performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers memoization, stable callbacks, component memoization, and lazy loading.

faq.question: Does it include mobile-specific UI patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes safe area handling and keyboard avoiding views.

faq.question: Is this skill tied to one AI tool?
faq.answer: No. It is described for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility.
